newsitem.title: UK: Tennis-Australia's Stoltenberg crashes at Queen's Club.
newsitem.headline: Tennis-Australia's Stoltenberg crashes at Queen's Club.

text.p: Australia's Jason Stoltenberg, who reached the last four at Wimbledon last year, was sent spinning out of the Queen's grasscourt tournament in Monday's first round by unheralded German Jens Knippschild.
World number 105 Knippschild eased past the 14th seed into the second round of the 422,000-pound sterling ($700,000) event with a 7-5 3-6 6-2 win in one hour 54 minutes.

"The last time I played on grass was a boys' tournament in Rosmalen (Netherlands) so I am obviously very pleased," the 22-year-old German said. "I'm surprised though because I have so little experience on grass."
Britain's Martin Lee dumped Russian Davis Cup player Andrei Olhovskiy out of the tournament in a three-set turnaround.
The former junior world number one lost the opening set of his match 0-6 before snatching the second two 6-4 6-4. "I was just very, very nervous before the start of the match," Lee said.
Javier Frana of Argentina squeezed past Frenchman Arnaud Boetsch 7-6 7-6 to book a second-round appointment with world number one Pete Sampras of the United States on Wednesday.
Scott Draper beat fellow Australian Sandon Stolle 6-7 6-4 6-4 and was rewarded with a second-round clash against second-ranked American Michael Chang.
Briton Andrew Richardson, who stands two metres tall, came back from a set down to beat Armenian Sargis Sargsian and now faces friend and fourth seed Tim Henman in Tuesday's second round.

Sixth seed Mark Philippoussis also plays on Tuesday. The Australian big-server, nicknamed the Scud, meets Jonathan Stark after the American won his first round over South African Neville Godwin 7-5 7-6.
